textbookText: Plants which grow in wet places or grow either partially or completely submerged in water are commonly referred to as hydrophytes or aquatic plants. Examples: Hydrilla, Pistia, Eichornia, Lemna, etc.
According to their distribution in a fresh water body, there are five categories of hydrophytes:
a. Free-floating These are the aquatic plant that float freely on water surface. They remain in contact with water and air, nut not soil. Example: Pistia, Eichornia, Lemna, etc.

b. Rooted with floating leaves These are the aquatic plants whose roots are fixed in mud but leaves have long petioles which keep floating on the water surface. Rest of the plant body is submerged in water. Example: Marsilea, Trapa, etc.
c. Submerged floating These are the aquatic plants that remain in contact only with water. They are not rooted in the mud and being completely submerged in water. Example: Najas, Ceratophyllum, etc.
d. Rooted submerged These are the hydrophytes that remain completely submerged in water, but rooted in the soil. Example: Hydrilla, Chara, etc.

e. Rooted emergent These hydrophytes grow in shallow waters and require excess of water but their shoots are partly or completely exposed to air. The root system is completely under water, fixed in soil. Example: Sagittaria, Ranunculus, Typha, etc.
